steps.title: Establish the common experiential operating model and partnership baseline
steps.summary: Undertake the institutional review already planned for 2.2.2 and use it to establish the common operating model for experiential opportunity. Map how King’s currently creates, holds, manages and activates external relationships across faculties, Careers & Employability, SASD, IES, Advancement and Alumni and other relevant areas. Examine staffing, systems and data, partner ownership, contracting, payments, safeguarding, risk, recruitment, accessibility, student support, promotion, evaluation and partner experience. Define the shared process through which experiential opportunities are sourced, designed, approved, promoted, delivered, supported and evaluated, with common templates, agreements and standards where these reduce duplication. Delivery remains distributed; the operating model should make local activity easier, safer and more consistent rather than centralising it.

outputs.title: Institutional partnership and capability baseline
outputs.summary: A current-state map of significant relationship-holding activity, staffing, systems, operational routes and partner-facing processes across King’s, identifying strengths, duplication, gaps, friction and underused capacity.

outputs.title: Common experiential opportunity operating model
outputs.summary: A proportionate institutional framework covering source, design, approval, promotion, delivery, support and evaluation, with clear roles, standards, templates, partner routes, data expectations and escalation points.

outputs.title: Future-demand scenarios
outputs.summary: Volume and complexity scenarios showing how partnership and operational demand could change as 2.1.4, 2.2.3 and 2.2.4 mature, so the £300,000 domestic experiential-infrastructure envelope can be translated into an appropriate workforce and operating model.

existingCapacity.role: Existing Careers & Employability, Work-Based Experience and partnership teams
existingCapacity.contribution: Provide operational knowledge, relationship intelligence and access to current processes, including domestic and international employer engagement, experiential delivery and existing faculty-facing support.
existingCapacity.owner: Careers & Employability, SASD, faculties and other relevant relationship-holding teams
existingCapacity.riskIfMissing: The operating model will not establish a sufficiently complete picture of current capability or the capacity that can be aligned before further investment is mobilised.

existingCapacity.role: Legal, procurement, finance, risk, data and student-support specialists
existingCapacity.contribution: Help define proportionate shared routes for agreements, payments, risk, safeguarding, data, accessibility and support without duplicating specialist institutional functions.
existingCapacity.riskIfMissing: The model may shift administrative burden rather than remove it and will struggle to scale safely.

enablingConditions.condition: Participation from all significant relationship-holding areas across King’s
enablingConditions.whatItUnlocks: A genuinely institution-wide baseline and operating model rather than a partial map of centrally visible activity.
enablingConditions.riskIfMissing: The model may duplicate existing capability, miss important partner networks or underestimate operational complexity.

steps.title: Mobilise the first phase of international employer engagement
steps.summary: Recruit and bring on stream the first two dedicated international employer-engagement roles: a G6 Employer Relations & Insights Manager (International) and a G5 Employer Relations & Insights Adviser focused on East Asia. Protect the existing East Asia portfolio, preserve hard-won employer relationships and consortium participation, maintain in-country activity and market intelligence, and build the management and operating foundations for later regional expansion. Introduce the £50,000 annual international non-pay envelope in step with the activity plan, with use tied to employer-facing and in-country activity rather than treated as a general travel budget.

outputs.title: Protected East Asia employer-engagement capability
outputs.summary: Dedicated staff own and sustain the existing East Asia employer portfolio, market intelligence, employer activity and international-student employment support.

outputs.title: International employer-engagement plan and pipeline
outputs.summary: A regional employer pipeline, relationship plan, activity calendar and evidence framework ready to support later expansion into South and South East Asia, Europe and North America.

newInvestment.periodNeeded: Immediate mobilisation from October 2026; annualised cost shown
newInvestment.fundingRoute: King’s Edge / Education and Student Success mobilisation investment, with wider recruitment and reputation benefits recognised outside the portfolio
newInvestment.rationale: Provides dedicated leadership, coordination, market insight and relationship ownership for international employer engagement, protecting existing East Asia activity and preparing regional expansion.
newInvestment.riskIfMissing: Existing international employer relationships and market presence remain fragile, current activity continues to displace domestic capacity, and King’s risks losing momentum in strategically important markets.

newInvestment.item: G5 Employer Relations & Insights Adviser (East Asia)
newInvestment.periodNeeded: Immediate mobilisation from October 2026; annualised cost shown
newInvestment.fundingRoute: King’s Edge / Education and Student Success mobilisation investment, with wider recruitment and reputation benefits recognised outside the portfolio
newInvestment.rationale: Provides dedicated regional capacity to sustain and deepen the proven East Asia portfolio and support students and graduates seeking employment outcomes in that market.
newInvestment.riskIfMissing: East Asia activity remains dependent on discretionary capacity and hard-won employer relationships and market credibility may be lost.

newInvestment.fundingRoute: King’s Edge / Education and Student Success mobilisation investment, with activity coordinated with Global Student Recruitment and Admissions
newInvestment.rationale: Funds the employer-facing and in-country activity required to make the international staffing capability productive across priority markets.
newInvestment.riskIfMissing: Dedicated staff will have limited ability to convert relationships and market intelligence into visible employer activity, opportunities and recruitment-facing value.

enablingConditions.condition: Ongoing alignment with Global Student Recruitment and Admissions on priority markets and recruitment-facing employability needs
enablingConditions.whatItUnlocks: A shared market strategy and explicit tracking of benefits that flow into attraction, conversion and reputation as well as graduate outcomes.
enablingConditions.riskIfMissing: International employability activity may become disconnected from wider institutional market priorities and shared benefits will be harder to evidence.

steps.title: Review student opportunity funding and philanthropic growth routes
steps.summary: Preserve the existing 2.2.2 access-and-opportunity-growth work. Map and review the financial support currently available for students undertaking employment-enhancing and developmental activity, including centrally and locally held funds and externally supported schemes. Develop options for a coherent Student Opportunities Fund focused on low-friction £150-£250 microbursaries and more substantial awards of around £4,000 for genuine out-of-pocket participation costs. In parallel, work with alumni and philanthropy colleagues to develop propositions that increase opportunity supply as well as access, including service-learning and social-good models in which paid PhD project leads mobilise flexible opportunities for wider student participation. The design work sits within King’s Edge, but any new Student Opportunities Fund award pot is outside the King’s Edge mobilisation ask and requires a separate funding, consolidation or philanthropic route.

outputs.title: Student opportunity funding landscape and consolidation options
outputs.summary: A review of current funding pots, eligibility, administration, restrictions, student use and access friction, with options for consolidation into a simpler and more coherent Student Opportunities Fund.

outputs.title: Student Opportunities Fund design options
outputs.summary: Options for low-friction microbursaries of around £150-£250 and larger awards of around £4,000 for genuine participation costs, including eligibility, administration, potential consolidation or external-funding routes and boundaries between financial access support and educational provision.

outputs.title: Alumni and philanthropic opportunity-growth propositions
outputs.summary: Investable propositions through which alumni relationships and philanthropic capital can increase both access to opportunity and the supply of new opportunity, including a developed service-learning and social-good model using paid PhD project-mobilisation roles.

existingCapacity.role: Existing student-funding, Alumni, Advancement and Philanthropy capacity
existingCapacity.contribution: Provide the current funding landscape, donor and alumni context, administrative insight and specialist input needed to develop consolidation and growth options.
existingCapacity.owner: Relevant student-support, Advancement, Alumni and Philanthropy teams
existingCapacity.riskIfMissing: The review may design new mechanisms without understanding current restrictions, administration or realistic philanthropic routes.

enablingConditions.condition: Visibility of current student opportunity funds, external schemes and donor restrictions
enablingConditions.whatItUnlocks: A credible consolidation proposal and a clear distinction between funding that can be pooled, aligned or must remain restricted.
enablingConditions.riskIfMissing: The proposed Student Opportunities Fund may be financially or legally unrealistic.

assumptions.title: Student Opportunities Fund awards are outside the King’s Edge mobilisation ask
assumptions.summary: The design and consolidation work sits within 2.2.2, but any new award pot requires a separate institutional, consolidated-fund, philanthropic or other approved funding route.

steps.title: Design the proactive Graduate Transitions operating model
steps.summary: Design the operating model for a small Graduate Transitions function ahead of a May 2027 launch. Define priority graduate cohorts and targeting logic, agree how Careers Readiness and other relevant evidence will identify graduates who may benefit from intervention, establish handover and referral routes from student-facing careers support, define coaching and case-management approaches, connect employer-referral and international-graduate routes, and agree a proportionate benefits and evaluation framework.

outputs.title: Graduate Transitions service design
outputs.summary: A bounded operating model covering targeting, outreach, coaching, job-search support, employer referral, international-graduate support, escalation and handover from student-facing careers provision.

outputs.title: Graduate Transitions evidence and benefits baseline
outputs.summary: Baseline measures and an evaluation design covering reach, engagement, progression, positive destinations, highly skilled and meaningful outcomes, priority groups and international graduates.

existingCapacity.role: Careers & Employability leadership, Careers Readiness data and existing graduate-access provision
existingCapacity.contribution: Provide service-design expertise, data access, referral routes and the current two-year graduate-access baseline from which the proactive model will be built.
existingCapacity.riskIfMissing: The new team may become an additional reactive service rather than a targeted graduate-success function.

enablingConditions.condition: Appropriate access to Careers Readiness and graduate-contact data, with agreed privacy, targeting and outreach rules
enablingConditions.whatItUnlocks: Proactive identification and contact of graduates who may be at greater risk of poorer outcomes.
enablingConditions.riskIfMissing: The service will be unable to move materially beyond self-referral.

steps.title: Launch the Graduate Transitions / Early Careers team
steps.summary: Bring the Graduate Transitions capability on stream from May 2027 with a deliberately bounded initial team of one G7 Head of Graduate Transitions and one G6 Graduate Transitions Coach. Use proactive outreach to priority graduates, personalised career planning and coaching, job-search and recruitment support, employer referrals and targeted interventions for graduates facing additional barriers. Use evidence from delivery to determine the scale and shape of any longer-term model rather than assuming the larger four-post structure originally proposed.

outputs.title: Operational Graduate Transitions service
outputs.summary: A two-person team is live from May 2027 and actively supports priority graduates through the post-completion transition.

outputs.title: Graduate transition insight loop
outputs.summary: Recurring evidence about where graduates struggle is fed back into purpose, experiential, employer-engagement and student-facing careers provision.

newInvestment.fundingRoute: King’s Edge / Education and Student Success mobilisation investment
newInvestment.rationale: Creates accountable leadership for the proactive graduate-success model, targeting, case-management approach, employer referral and evidence of impact.
newInvestment.riskIfMissing: Graduate support remains largely reactive and King’s lacks dedicated ownership for targeted intervention through the Graduate Outcomes period.

newInvestment.fundingRoute: King’s Edge / Education and Student Success mobilisation investment
newInvestment.rationale: Provides direct coaching, job-search, recruitment and employer-referral capacity for graduates identified through the proactive model.
newInvestment.riskIfMissing: The service will have leadership but insufficient direct delivery capacity to support priority graduates at useful scale.

steps.title: Complete the international employer-engagement team
steps.summary: From September 2027, add two further G5 Employer Relations & Insights Advisers to extend the international employer-engagement model into South and South East Asia and Europe and North America. Use the Phase 1 pipeline, market insight and operating model to sequence activity, protect domestic employer-engagement capacity and connect the international portfolio explicitly to both graduate-success and institutional recruitment priorities.

outputs.title: Full international employer-engagement capability
outputs.summary: The international team reaches its planned structure of one G6 and three G5 roles, with defined regional portfolios and a common approach to employer relations, market insight and student/graduate opportunity.

outputs.title: Cross-institutional international employability benefits framework
outputs.summary: Graduate-outcome, employer-engagement, recruitment, conversion and reputation benefits are tracked explicitly, including benefits realised outside Education and Student Success.

newInvestment.item: G5 Employer Relations & Insights Adviser (South & South East Asia)
newInvestment.fundingRoute: King’s Edge / Education and Student Success mobilisation investment, with wider recruitment and reputation benefits recognised outside the portfolio
newInvestment.rationale: Extends dedicated employer-engagement and market-intelligence capacity into a priority set of international markets, including India and wider South and South East Asia.
newInvestment.riskIfMissing: The international proposition remains concentrated in East Asia and King’s underuses employability as part of its recruitment and graduate-success strategy in other priority markets.

newInvestment.item: G5 Employer Relations & Insights Adviser (Europe & North America)
newInvestment.fundingRoute: King’s Edge / Education and Student Success mobilisation investment, with wider recruitment and reputation benefits recognised outside the portfolio
newInvestment.rationale: Extends employer relationship, opportunity development and market intelligence across Europe and North America.
newInvestment.riskIfMissing: King’s lacks dedicated capacity to develop and sustain employer relationships in these markets and cannot realise the full strategic benefit of the international employability model.

assumptions.title: The specified careers and employability package is £390,354 annualised
assumptions.summary: When all six new posts are on stream, annualised staffing is £340,354. Together with the £50,000 international non-pay envelope, the specified international employer-engagement and Graduate Transitions package totals £390,354. This sits alongside, rather than replacing, the £300,000 p.a. domestic experiential opportunity translation and partnership-infrastructure envelope.

steps.title: Mobilise and mature domestic experiential opportunity translation infrastructure
steps.summary: From 2027/28, mobilise a reduced £300,000 p.a. Core envelope for general domestic experiential opportunity translation and partnership infrastructure. Use the Year 1 operating-model and demand work to determine the most effective mix of faculty-facing brokerage and shared operational capacity. The purpose is to turn UK employer, alumni, civic, cultural, community and other external relationships into student-ready experiential opportunities by supporting scoping, brokerage, learning-design translation, contracting, partner onboarding, payments, administration and handover into 2.1.4, 2.2.3 and 2.2.4. Alongside mobilisation, operate and evaluate the combined infrastructure through the principal growth years of King’s Edge, tracking partner experience, opportunity throughput, international employer relationships, Graduate Transitions progression, financial-access demand and wider recruitment and reputation benefits. Grow alumni and philanthropic contribution and expand any separately funded Student Opportunities Fund where evidence supports it.

outputs.title: Domestic experiential opportunity translation capacity mobilised
outputs.summary: A demand-informed mix of faculty-facing and shared operational capability is in place to convert domestic external relationships and propositions into well-formed student opportunities.

outputs.title: Integrated employability and experiential infrastructure review
outputs.summary: Regular evidence reviews compare opportunity throughput, partner and graduate outcomes, operational friction and cross-institutional benefits against the capacity in place.

outputs.title: Evidence-led recurrent operating model
outputs.summary: King’s confirms the enduring workforce and service model, including what should transfer into business as usual, what can be repurposed and whether the £300,000 domestic envelope remains the right level as demand matures.

outputs.title: Scaled access and philanthropic mechanisms
outputs.summary: Any separately funded Student Opportunities Fund, alumni contribution and philanthropic opportunity-creation mechanisms grow in response to evidence, with repeatable models retained where they demonstrate value.

existingCapacity.role: Existing partnership, Work-Based Experience and specialist-service capacity
existingCapacity.contribution: Operate alongside the new domestic translation envelope, ensuring the investment builds on and aligns existing capability rather than duplicating it.
existingCapacity.owner: Careers & Employability, SASD, faculties and relevant institutional partners
existingCapacity.riskIfMissing: The £300,000 envelope will buy less incremental capability if it has to recreate functions and expertise that already exist elsewhere in King’s.

newInvestment.item: Domestic experiential opportunity translation and partnership-infrastructure envelope
newInvestment.category: domestic experiential partnership and operational capacity
newInvestment.periodNeeded: 2027/28 onward; mobilisation-funded in 2027/28 and 2028/29, with intended transfer into business as usual thereafter
newInvestment.fundingRoute: King’s Edge mobilisation investment for Years 2 and 3, with intended recurrent BAU settlement thereafter
newInvestment.fundingStatus: Core planning assumption, subject to review and approval
newInvestment.rationale: Provides general domestic faculty-facing brokerage and shared operational capacity to translate UK employer and other external relationships into student-ready experiential opportunities. The exact grade and role mix should be recommended from the Year 1 capability review and tested against demand from 2.1.4, 2.2.3 and 2.2.4.
newInvestment.riskIfMissing: King’s may grow curricular, near-curriculum and flexible experiential ambition without sufficient domestic capacity to source, scope, broker, contract, administer and sustain the external opportunities required to deliver it.

enablingConditions.condition: Authority to align or repurpose existing partnership and specialist-service capacity around the common operating model
enablingConditions.whatItUnlocks: A stronger domestic opportunity-translation model within the £300,000 envelope by combining new investment with existing institutional capability.
enablingConditions.riskIfMissing: The same investment will buy less partnership-facing and opportunity-translation capacity.

enablingConditions.condition: Benefits data can distinguish Education and Student Success outcomes from wider recruitment, conversion and reputation effects
enablingConditions.whatItUnlocks: A more credible institutional value case and clearer shared ownership of benefits that sit outside the funding portfolio.
enablingConditions.riskIfMissing: The full institutional return may be under-recognised and the investment may be judged only against a subset of the benefits it creates.

assumptions.title: Fully mobilised annualised 2.2.2 Core ask is £690,354
assumptions.summary: The £300,000 p.a. domestic experiential opportunity translation and partnership-infrastructure envelope sits alongside the £390,354 annualised international employer-engagement and Graduate Transitions package, giving a fully mobilised annualised Core ask of £690,354. Any Student Opportunities Fund award pot remains separate and is not included.
